Q: Visual Studio Code is showing only one file in the tab bar (can't open multiple files) A:

In my case, the editor limit is set to true in file settings.json. Change it to a false value:

"workbench.editor.limit.enabled": false

If you want to allow only a maximum of five tabs to open, you can set

"workbench.editor.limit.enabled": true,
"workbench.editor.limit.value": 5,

Q: How to round very big float number into x numbers after decimal point in Scheme? A:

I came up with this solution. I've split the number into integer and fraction and then rounded the fraction with 4 numbers after decimal point. The bigger value than 4 didn't work for me.

(define (round-fixed x . rest)
  "(round-fixed x)

   Rounds a number to a given presition"
  (let* ((precision (if (null? rest) 14 (car rest)))
         (factor (** 10 precision)))
    (if (> (abs x) 1000) ;; arbitrary big number
        (let-values (((int float) (split-number x)))
          (+ int (round-fixed float 4))) ;; arbitrary precision
        (/ (Math.round (* x factor))
           (exact->inexact factor)))))

(define (split-number x)
  "(split-number x)

   Split float number into integer and fraction value."
  (let* ((a (Math.round x))
         (b (- x a)))
    (values a b)))

Q: Counter implementation unexpected behaviour A:

It looks like the clk is typod and it was a sync reset, rather than an async.

Try this :

module clock_test(
  input        clk_in,
  input        rst,
  output [7:0] led
);

reg [23:0] counter;

assign led = counter[23:16];

always @(posedge clk_in or posedge rst)  begin
  if(rst) begin
    counter <= 0;
  end
  else begin
    counter <= counter +1;
  end
 end
 endmodule // clock_test

NB: you are using an active high reset (1 implies reset). If you are actually using active low (0 applies reset) the you need to change the following:

always @(posedge clk_in or negedge rst)  begin
  if(~rst) begin
    counter <= 0;

Q: Hog mode / Exclusive access to audio output device with SoX A:

SoX doesn't hog audio devices; it just uses them, but if on Linux you use the "oss" audio driver, that hogs the audio device.

On Mac OS which only has "coreaudio" you're probably stuck.
